architecture.summary: The complete S1-01/S1-02/S1-03a/S1-03b/S1-04a stack retires customer grant writes and uses two hosted roles: User gives product/MCP access; Admin includes that access and administration. Current active memberships and validated role catalogs authorize requests. Default, retired, unknown, inactive, missing, and foreign grants cannot authorize access. Administration has no MFA precondition, and legacy inferred MFA values normalize to false while session/cookie formats remain compatible. Active product-member counts include each unique authorized membership once. The stack introduces neutral identity session/profile and signup contracts. Named signup requires canonical organization-purpose documents and a verified creator. A confirmed new organization and reread must match its name, identity, and ten-field v2 authority/legal record before the initial Admin write. The membership response and a current read must confirm that Admin/product access. Retained v1/v2 records are read-only replay barriers; they cannot restore grants or convert personal consent. The signup route selects the confirmed organization, preserves cookie ordering and cancellation, then opens its MCP guide. A neutral callback supplies the exact active-membership name to portal JSON; missing names fail safely and names render as text. CSRF/origin checks, bounded admission, safe failures, native invitations, and browser/MCP organization isolation remain. The unchanged personal production bundle cannot enable new creation; approved organization wording and live cutover checks remain S1-05. No provider setting, new datastore, infrastructure, SDK dependency, or resource lifetime changes. The registry records these component/runtime guarantees; the member-read runtime diagram now shows the combined complete overviews; other parent diagrams remain accurate. The web-to-organizations owner pair is declared runtime because the form calls its public name validator; forbidden edges and the declared public-module list remain. Signup adapter tests move to integration for that real collaboration. Required gate selection and approval rules remain; the image assertion now checks the legacy-bundle refusal. Observable authorization, persistence, and portal/server contracts require T2 Need architect. Internal interfaces, sensitive paths, the dependency declaration, and retained quality findings also require human review. No new decision record was requested. S1-03b adds recovery and eligibility characterization through the unchanged production interfaces. It covers lost and late writes, two application instances racing with different names, a held winning response, restart, failed browser selection, malformed records, legacy User preservation, former-invite eligibility, and other current workspace access. A narrow test-only exact-route interceptor preserves fake persistence while delaying or dropping its response. No additional production contract, dependency, resource lifetime, or registry diagram changes arise from S1-03b. S1-04a combines active members and pending native invitations on Members, with one email/User/Admin radio form and authorized legacy-URL redirect. Required neutral projection fields carry the provider subject, expiry, and the selected organization name from the existing current authorization read. No new provider call is added for that name. The portal shows Members from current access roles; the route independently checks current Admin authority. Both bounded reads must succeed before rendering. A neutral UnconfirmedChangeError distinguishes a started write from failed preflight; the server gives a fixed 503 with a status-only GET link and never repeats the write or equates pending with email delivery. Origin/CSRF/current-role/current-target checks remain. Provider cause and invitation credentials stay out of the page. The current HTTP/UI and internal projection/error contracts change, but there is no new owner, datastore, SDK method, dependency, lifecycle or deployment change. Members uses native HTML forms and hashed inline styles; current navigation keeps the existing selector. S1-04b retains native acceptance and live preservation proof; S1-05 retains legal/cutover holds. S1-04b adds default sign-in landing: an absent sealed destination differs from an explicit safe return, including the root; old explicit-destination envelopes remain valid. The browser adapter returns neutral trusted identity from validated exchange facts. Session routes reuse the supplied AccessResolver and open the portal only for a matching current product-authorized selection. No trusted selection or stale selection opens the existing selector without choosing an organization. A post-exchange read failure keeps completed cookie effects and offers a selector recovery link, with no code replay. Explicit returns keep existing route checks. Browser selection cannot rebind MCP tokens. The registry adds the ordered callback runtime view and updates the neutral session contract text. These HTTP/internal contracts require T2 review; no SDK operation, provider setting, new owner, storage, dependency or resource lifetime changes. Native acceptance and role-preservation/race proofs remain unrun with explicit environment holds; the prepared matrix is not a provider pass. The stack includes the shared developer metrics repair from PR #230 and behavior-preserving Members rendering refactor. Direct session cancellation and post-exchange landing cancellation now have separate specifications. Each waits for entry, aborts, checks the exact abort reason before settling the provider, and observes a later failure without reporting it. Application contracts and numeric goals remain unchanged by these repairs. The callback registry view now separates provider facts from local session validation and the web landing decision. It shows the membership and catalog reads with their local validation gates. The inherited Members view shows the two overview calls in their actual order. These map corrections describe existing behavior; they add no runtime change.
